Most FATAL Log Entries come from KERNEL (about 73%), with APP second (about 27%); no other Component comes close.

## Observed Facts
**Data Scope for every count below:** Dataset BGL, the whole period from 2005-06-03 15:42:50 to 2006-01-04 08:00:05 [E1], filtered to `level = FATAL`, with no message or Component filter.

- **Total:** 855,195 FATAL Log Entries [E2]. Only 4 Components produced any:

| Rank | Component | FATAL Log Entries | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | KERNEL | 626,450 [E2] | ~73% |
| 2 | APP | 228,536 [E2] | ~27% |
| 3 | LINKCARD | 206 [E2] | <0.1% |
| 4 | MMCS | 3 [E2] | ~0% |

- **By month, it's very uneven:** June 2005 has 548,475 [E3], about 64% of the total. After that the monthly counts are 19,769 (Jul), 69,452 (Aug), 81,818 (Sep), 42,542 (Oct), 47,641 (Nov) and 44,859 (Dec) [E3]. January 2006 has only 639 [E3], but the data stops on Jan 4.
- **By alert tag (all Components):** 506,797 FATAL Log Entries have no alert tag ("-") [E4]. The largest tagged groups are KERNDTLB 152,734, KERNSTOR 63,491, APPSEV 49,651, KERNMNTF 31,531 and KERNTERM 23,338 [E4]. There are 37 tags in total; I only looked at the top 10 [E4].

## Hypotheses
- June 2005 probably holds a short burst of repeated messages, not a steady failure rate. If so, the overall ranking may say more about one noisy period than about a problem that keeps coming back.
- After June, FATAL volume stays fairly steady at about 40k–80k per month from Aug to Dec [E3]. KERNEL problems (KERNDTLB, KERNSTOR, KERNMNTF) probably make up most of that ongoing volume, but I haven't split the months by Component, so this is unconfirmed.

## Unknowns
- **How many actual incidents these represent:** one failure can log thousands of lines, so these counts can't tell us that.
- **Which Component caused the June 2005 spike:** I didn't break the monthly trend down by Component.
- **What the 506,797 untagged FATAL Log Entries [E4] are:** without a tag, their failure type isn't known.
- **Whether a few nodes produce most of the volume:** I haven't grouped by node yet.

## Next Step
Start with KERNEL, since it has the most FATAL Log Entries:
1. Run a daily trend of KERNEL FATAL Log Entries for June 2005 to see whether the spike is one burst or keeps recurring.
2. Count KERNEL FATAL Log Entries by node to see if a few nodes dominate.
3. Then check whether KERNDTLB keeps recurring from Aug to Dec 2005, before moving on to APP (APPSEV).
